writeup: TIC 342586820 is a newly discovered eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 1.9511 days. When the primary star passes in front of its companion, the system dims by 2.93 percent - a signal detected with very high confidence in the TESS data. However, no secondary eclipse was observed. The star does not appear in any of six major variable-star catalogs, making it a genuinely novel discovery. While the detection itself is robust, there is an important caveat: the star's position on the detector is very close to a brighter neighbor star, and TESS's resolution cannot confidently separate the two. This means the dimming signal might partially come from the neighboring star rather than exclusively from TIC 342586820 itself.
